chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man emerged from a ship naked or his clothes were stripped off and he found nothing to pray in. He said: 'He prays by nodding. And if it is a woman, she places her hand over her private part, and if it is a man, he places his hand over his private part. Then they sit and nod by nodding, and they do not bow and they do not prostrate, so that what is behind them becomes exposed; their prayer is by nodding with their heads.' He said: 'And if they are in water or a deep sea, they do not prostrate in it, and facing is removed from them, so they nod in that; their raising [of hands/head] is facing and their placing [of hands/head] is facing.'

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: Nodding (gesturing with head or hand) as a substitute for full physical movements in prayer

ai.seo_question: How does one perform prayer if they have no clothes to wear?
ai.summary: Recorded by Zurara and transmitted through the chain of al-Tusi, this hadith details the concession (rukhsa) for prayer when clothing is entirely absent, mandating that both men and women cover their private parts with their hands while performing prayer via nodding (ima') without bowing or prostrating. It further clarifies that in open water, the obligation to face the Qibla is lifted, emphasizing the principle of ease in ritual purity and posture during extreme necessity.
